sections.title: What is happening now
sections.intro_md:
The years 2025 and 2026 changed Tamil Nadu's politics more than any since 1967.

In **January 2025**, Chief Minister **M. K. Stalin** announced that iron objects from **Sivagalai** had been dated to about **3345 BCE**, which would make Tamil Nadu one of the earliest places in the world to work iron. Archaeologists outside the state asked to see peer-reviewed results. In **April 2025**, the **Supreme Court** ruled that Governor R. N. Ravi had acted illegally by sitting on ten bills passed by the assembly, and set time limits for governors. The new **Pamban bridge** opened the same month. A row with the ASI over Keeladi's final report ran through 2025.

The defining event was the 2026 election. In **September 2025**, a crush at a rally of actor **Vijay**'s party, the **TVK**, in **Karur** killed **41** people. Seven months later, on **23 April 2026**, Tamil Nadu voted with a record **85.1%** turnout, and on **4 May** TVK won **108 of 234 seats**, ending 59 years of DMK and AIADMK rule.

spotlights.name: C. Joseph Vijay
spotlights.spot_it: A slim actor with a neat beard, often in a white shirt, waving from the roof of a campaign bus.
spotlights.story_md: Vijay, called **Thalapathy** ('commander'), was one of Tamil cinema's top-earning stars, with films such as *Ghilli*, *Mersal* and *Leo*. He founded **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam** in **February 2024** and said he would quit acting. TVK contested alone, won **108 seats** with about **35%** of the vote, and Vijay won both seats he contested, Perambur and Tiruchirappalli East. Short of the 118 needed, he formed a government with **Congress**, later backed by the Left parties, the VCK and the IUML. He was sworn in on **10 May 2026** as Tamil Nadu's 22nd chief minister. Stalin lost his own seat, Kolathur.
spotlights.why_it_matters: He broke the two-party Dravidian system in his first election.
spotlights.memory_hook: Thalapathy: a star's first election, a 59-year streak broken.

spotlights.name: M. K. Stalin
spotlights.spot_it: A man with dark-tinted glasses and a black-and-white moustache, in a white shirt with a DMK-striped veshti.
spotlights.story_md: Named after the Soviet leader, who died days after his birth in 1953, Stalin is Karunanidhi's son. He was Chennai's mayor from **1996**, deputy chief minister from 2009, and chief minister from **2021**. His government launched the **breakfast scheme** (2022), free bus travel for women and ₹1,000 a month to women heads of households (2023). He led the states' fight on Hindi, the national education policy, delimitation and governors' powers. In **2026** his DMK fell to 59 seats, and he lost his own seat.
spotlights.why_it_matters: He defined the DMK's federalist politics in the 2020s.
spotlights.memory_hook: Named after a Soviet leader, beaten by a film star.

sections.title: Recap
sections.intro_md:
Tamil Nadu is India's southeastern corner, **72 million** people, the **second largest economy** among states, and a culture that has written in one language for more than **2,000 years**.

- **Old towns, old script:** Keeladi pushes Tamil urban life back to around the 6th century BCE, and Tamil-Brahmi pots reached Egypt.
- **Kings in stone:** the Pallavas carved Mamallapuram; the Cholas built Thanjavur's Big Temple in 1010 and sent a navy to Southeast Asia.
- **Gopurams:** Meenakshi in Madurai, Srirangam's 73 m tower, Rameswaram's kilometre of corridors.
- **A Dravidian century:** Periyar, Annadurai, the 1965 language agitation, the 1969 renaming, and the school meal.
- **Arts:** Bharatanatyam, the December season, nadaswaram, parai.
- **Crafts:** Kanchipuram silk, Thanjavur paintings and dolls, Swamimalai bronzes.
- **Food:** idli, dosa, filter coffee, the banana leaf meal.
- **Film and power:** six chief ministers from cinema, the latest Vijay in 2026.
- **Economy:** the Detroit of Asia, Tiruppur's T-shirts, Sivakasi's fireworks.

Tomorrow, try to recall the three crowned kings and the six film-world chief ministers.

best_facts.fact: Since 1967, every elected Tamil Nadu government was led by the DMK or AIADMK, until actor Vijay's TVK won 108 seats in May 2026, in its first election.
best_facts.why_surprising: A 59-year two-party lock broke in one vote.

best_facts.fact: Six Tamil Nadu chief ministers have had film careers: Annadurai, Karunanidhi, MGR, Janaki Ramachandran, Jayalalithaa and Vijay.
best_facts.why_surprising: No other state has given screenwriters and stars this much power.

best_facts.fact: A potsherd inscribed in Tamil-Brahmi has been found at Berenike, a Roman port on Egypt's Red Sea coast.
best_facts.why_surprising: Tamil writing travelled to Egypt 2,000 years ago.

best_facts.fact: The Thiruvalluvar statue at Kanyakumari is 133 feet tall, one foot for each chapter of the Tirukkural.
The tallest minaret of Nagore Dargah was built by a Hindu king, Pratap Singh of Thanjavur.
best_facts.why_surprising: A Sufi shrine built with Hindu royal money.

best_facts.fact: Rajendra Chola I sent a navy across the Bay of Bengal to raid the Srivijaya empire in 1025.
best_facts.why_surprising: A rare overseas naval expedition by an Indian king.

best_facts.fact: Ramanujan was working as a clerk at the Madras Port Trust when he wrote to G. H. Hardy in 1913.
best_facts.why_surprising: A port clerk became one of history's great mathematicians.

best_facts.fact: MGR was born in Kandy, Sri Lanka, and after being shot in the neck in 1967, a photo of him in hospital helped the DMK win that year.
best_facts.why_surprising: A bullet wound became an election poster.

best_facts.fact: Elihu Yale made his fortune as governor of Madras, then funded the college that became Yale University.
best_facts.why_surprising: An Ivy League name came from Chennai money.

best_facts.fact: In 2014, after a club refused entry to a High Court judge in a veshti, Tamil Nadu passed a law banning such dress codes.
best_facts.why_surprising: A dress code dispute became law.

best_facts.fact: The Descent of the Ganges relief at Mamallapuram includes a cat standing in mock penance while mice gather.
Thaipusam, a Tamil festival, draws about a million people to Batu Caves in Malaysia, more than any site in India.
best_facts.why_surprising: The festival's centre has moved abroad.

best_facts.fact: The Mudumalai couple in The Elephant Whisperers won India its first Oscar for best documentary short in 2023.
best_facts.why_surprising: An orphan elephant calf reached the Oscars.

best_facts.fact: Thanjavur's Big Temple inscriptions list about 400 temple dancers by name and address.
best_facts.why_surprising: A thousand-year-old staff directory in stone.

best_facts.fact: The Srirangam Rajagopuram stood unfinished for about 400 years until 1987.
best_facts.why_surprising: A gateway four centuries in the making.

best_facts.fact: Madurai jasmine has had its own GI tag since 2013, and it is sold by the muzham, the length of a forearm.
best_facts.why_surprising: A flower measured by your arm.

best_facts.fact: Kudankulam is India's largest nuclear plant, and nearby Muppandal is one of Asia's largest wind farms.
best_facts.why_surprising: Atoms and wind on the same coast.

best_facts.fact: In January 2025 Tamil Nadu announced iron from Sivagalai dated to about 3345 BCE, a claim still awaiting peer review.
best_facts.why_surprising: It would rewrite the history of iron.

side_dish.title: The kolam as computer science
side_dish.body_md:
A Tamil kolam is drawn before sunrise, often around a grid of dots, with one line that loops without lifting the hand and ends where it started. That is a mathematical object. In the 1970s **Gift Siromoney**, a statistician at Madras Christian College, and his colleagues began treating kolams as **picture languages**: sets of shapes generated by simple rules, the way a grammar generates sentences. They wrote rules that could produce whole families of kolam patterns and used them to study how computers might recognise and generate images.

Later researchers showed that many single-line kolams trace a path that passes through every gap between dots exactly once, related to **Eulerian paths** in graph theory, and that some kolam families are fractal: each larger pattern repeats smaller copies of itself. Others have used kolams to teach symmetry and recursion in schools.

The women who draw them learn this without equations. Grandmothers teach rules such as 'never leave the line open' and 'go around every dot', which turn out to be constraints a mathematician would write. So the next time you see a kolam on a doorstep, you are looking at an algorithm executed by hand, in rice flour, every day.

offline_task.title: Make a tumbler of filter coffee, the Tamil way
offline_task.body_md:
You need strong ground coffee (ideally with 10 to 20% chicory), boiled milk and sugar. If you do not have a South Indian filter, use a French press with very little water.

1. Put 3 heaped spoons of coffee in the top chamber, press lightly, and pour in about 100 ml of boiling water. Wait 15 minutes for a thick decoction to drip down.
2. Heat 200 ml of milk until it just boils.
3. In a steel tumbler or tall cup, add 2 to 3 spoons of decoction, sugar to taste, then the hot milk.
4. Pour the coffee between the tumbler and a wide bowl, raising your hand as you pour, four or five times. It cools, mixes and grows a froth.

Drink it from the tumbler without touching the rim to your lips, the way many Tamil households do. Notice the bitterness of chicory: it was once a way to stretch expensive coffee.
